title: Introduce latency-frontier detector with segmented-slice rollback and traffic shedder
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: We observed intermittent sub-percentile latency regressions that slip past our current canary because they are slice-local (only affecting a subset of traffic shapes and noisy by user cohort). This PR introduces a novel "latency-frontier" detector that computes per-slice rolling quantile frontiers and a segment-aware aggregation strategy to identify regressions that are masked by aggregate medians. The goal is to detect small but user-visible degradations earlier and attach a graceful traffic-shedding rollback path for high-severity slices.

What this PR does: adds a latency-frontier detector, a segmented sliding-window implementation, and an automated traffic shedder + rollback harness that ties into the existing canary orchestration. Key features:
- Rolling quantile frontier: track 50/90/95/99 per-slice percentiles with exponentially-weighted windowing and per-slice confidence scores.
- Slice scoring and prioritization: compute a combined anomaly score using signal magnitude, slice traffic weight, and historical volatility to prioritize probes and alerts.
- Segment-aware aggregation: avoid false positives by fusing neighboring slice signals using a locality kernel (temporal + similarity-based smoothing).
- Traffic shedder actuator: when the score and risk budget exceed thresholds, the actuator proposes a partial shed (route X% of the slice traffic to the previous stable model/tier) rather than full rollback.
- Rollback harness + telemetry: automatic rollback proposal creation in the canary controller with a human-in-the-loop confirm step; each proposal contains a compact causal trace and diffs for easier on-call decisioning.

Design notes: this approach trades earlier detection of small-impact regressions for slightly increased probe cost. The detector is conservative by default (higher thresholds) and exposes configuration knobs in the canary config (probe intensity, EWMA half-life, score weighting). We included safety gates to avoid oscillation (cooldown windows, hysteresis, and a minimum traffic floor for shedding).

Testing and validation: unit tests for the sliding-window quantile estimator; synthetic canary simulation harness to validate detection sensitivity and false positive rate across 10 traffic shapes; integration smoke against the canary controller in staging. We ran a 48h backtest on historical perf traces from 2025-11 to 2026-01 and measured a 42% improvement in detection lead time for targeted-slice regressions, with false positive rate kept under 0.6% at default thresholds.

Commits summary: ["init: latency-frontier core estimator and tests", "feat: slice scoring and aggregation pipeline", "feat: traffic-shedder actuator and canary controller hooks", "perf: optimize quantile estimator inner loop", "docs: config knobs and runbook additions"]

Changed areas (high level): ["perf-canary/src/detectors/latency_frontier.py", "perf-canary/src/actuators/traffic_shedder.py", "perf-canary/src/controller/rollback_harness.py", "perf-canary/tests/test_latency_frontier.py", "perf-canary/integration/simulations/segment_backtest.ipynb", "perf-canary/docs/runbooks/latency_frontier.md", "perf-canary/config/defaults/latency_frontier.yaml"]. The patch keeps changes localized to the perf-canary service and exposes a new canary config block; no changes to the runtime serving path.

Review conversation (summary):
- Ethan Rivers: "Nice design. Two concerns: 1) the EWMA half-life defaults look aggressive for low-traffic slices; 2) how do we ensure the shedder won't create a cascading capacity issue on the fallback tier?" Author: "Adjusted defaults to be more conservative (higher half-life) for slices under 100rps; added a fallback-capacity check to the actuator and a preflight that estimates downstream pressure. This is included in the last commit." 
- Sara Kim (SRE): "Can we add tracing hooks so oncall can quickly see which requests were shed and why?" Author: "Yes — added compact causal trace metadata on proposals and a small query in the controller UI to list recent shed events." 
- Luca Moretti: "Tests look good; suggest a chaos test where we induce rapid oscillation." Author: "Added a short chaos sim under integration that validates cooldown/hysteresis prevents oscillation in 10k-run randomized traffic scenarios." 
- Final review: approvals from Ethan and Sara after small nits fixed; Luca approved after rebase and additional test coverage.

CI checks and status: ["lint: pass", "unit-tests: pass (coverage 88.4%)", "integration: pass (staging run)", "benchmarks: pass (quantile estimator within perf budget)", "e2e: pass (canary controller smoke)"] — there was one transient failure on integration which re-ran and passed.

Deployment and rollout plan: merged to main and will be rolled out behind a feature flag for 20% of internal canaries next week. The plan:
1) feature-flagged staging -> monitor for 72h
2) enable for 20% internal canaries -> monitor 72h with elevated alerting
3) gradual ramp if no regressions; if triggered, the rollback harness will create a proposal for operator confirmation

Release notes: "Add latency-frontier detector and segmented traffic-shedder actuator for earlier detection and safe rollback of slice-local latency regressions. Feature-flagged; off by default."

Related work: builds on the slice-probing scaffolding (ENG-4401) and references runbook updates for operator workflows (ENG-5030).
